title: A `@check` can claim paths with `check.covers`; `check.scope` stays text and claims none
summary: Plan amendments C17 and C22. compliance-system's `@check` schema gains an optional check.covers, a list of text path selections, and documents check.scope, still required text, as what the check selects (the whole-workspace token *, a scope its evaluator reports, or prose). @inventarch/graph adds check.covers to CLAIM_FIELDS, so the claimant index, claimants(graph, path), db resolveSeat's claimants, db inertDeclarations, ia position's location seats and every other reader of claimants name a check whose covers selects a path, with field check.covers; a check's check.scope is still never a claim, even text that reads as a path, and claiming a path changes nothing about which verdicts ia validate binds the check to. A workspace that states no check.covers sees no change. The public vocabulary (docs/reference/language/vocabulary.json and .md, the CLI and door catalogues), the generated authoring reference for `@check` (shipped in @inventarch/authoring-system) and the authoring resource manifest are regenerated, and @inventarch/compliance-system ships the new schema, and the bundled inventarch/language base and the embedded host payload are rebuilt from the new schema, which moves the host payload pin. Limits: the native identities inventarch/language and compliance-system still read 1.2.0, the version 2.0.0 published with the previous schema bytes, so a native version move (as the 1.2.0 move did, with the public package inputs and system package policy) is needed before this is released; this change does not make it. Older CLIs refuse a workspace that states check.covers, as the closed schema they carry does not declare it.
